Assistant: Of course!  Here’s a recipe for Bourekas (often just called “bourekas”), a savory pastry made with phyllo dough and often filled with a meat or cheese.

Ingredients:
4 cups all-purpose flour
1 pound firm goat cheese, drained, grated (room temperature)
1/2 cup warm water
1 egg
1/2 tsp salt
1/4 tsp ground black pepper

Filling:
1/4 cup olive oil
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh basil

3-4 lbs beef or pork, diced into small cubes or patties

Salt
Pepper

Instructions:

1. In one large bowl, mix the dough ingredients well. Be very careful not to overwork the dough, as this will make the filling go crazy and make the dough tough.  Divide the dough in half and set one half aside.  Do not work with the other half at all.

2. On a lightly floured surface, roll out each half into a circle roughly 14 inches in diameter.  This should take about 10 minutes.  If the dough sticks to the surface, dust it with some flour.

3. Roll out the larger circle into a rectangle roughly 12 inches by 6 inches.

4. Spread the goat cheese over the dough, leaving a 1 inch border at the top and bottom.

5. Fold the dough in half, using the long edges of the dough to overlap each other.  Crease the fold to make a well in the center and pinch together the sides to seal.

6. Unfold the dough and cut off the top and bottom corners, leaving 1 inch all around the bottom.

7. Roll out each 1 inch strip into a thin circle.  Using a fork, prick the dough all over to relieve some of the pressure and prevent the pastry from tearing when you try to fold it back up.

8. Starting at one end, cross each strip over the previous strip and roll up the pastry tightly around the filling.

9. Pinch the edges, being careful to leave the top and bottom corners intact, and sprinkle with a little bit of salt and pepper.

10. Brush the top of the pastry with the olive oil, fold as before and tuck in the ends.  This should make two long rolls.  Place them on a parchment lined baking sheet.

11. Cut the long ends of the rolls and roll them in the flour to prevent them from sticking together.

12. Place the rolls in the oven and bake for about 10 minutes.  Turn down the oven to 400°F and bake for an additional 10 minutes or until the pastry is golden.  Remove from the oven and let rest for 5-10 minutes.

13. While the rolls rest, prepare the filling ingredients.  Heat the olive oil in a medium pan over medium heat.  Add the parsley and basil and stir for 1 minute.

14. Add the meat and seasoning to the pan and sauté for 5 minutes.  Remove from heat.

15. To assemble the bourekas, place a layer of phyllo on a flat surface, top with the meat and then cheese.  Fold the edges of the phyllo over the filling and fold up the phyllo.  Brush the top and bottom with egg wash and sprinkle with some more salt and pepper.  Roll up and cut into slices.

16. These are best served warm right away.
